title: F2: the family head trained with ATT&CK's own procedure examples added
question: Does adding ATT&CK's procedure examples (16,273 overlap-filtered sentences, 213 families) to F1's training data raise family top-1, above all on CTI-HAL?

data.train: F1's rows (cases_train.jsonl 6,308 + cases_annoctr_train.jsonl 1,453) + cases_attack_train.jsonl 16,273 = 24,034 rows, no reweighting
data.attack_rows: every active 'uses' relationship (group, software or campaign to a listed technique) with a description, citations and links stripped; identical texts merged (17,033 texts); dropped when they overlap a held-out text of public dev, public test, CTI-HAL, AnnoCTR dev or AnnoCTR test: 378 exact/near duplicates (token Jaccard >= 0.9), 243 containing a held-out text of 6+ tokens, 132 sharing a 10-token run, 7 repeats. Of the dropped, 613 matched TRAM (dev 290, test 323), 6 CTI-HAL, 1 derived procedures, 1 expert

fixed.init: cribl-ai/cribl-decision-1.0 adapter and a freshly initialised head, as F1 (not F1's checkpoint), so the data is the only change
fixed.training: as F1 (LoRA lr 1e-4, head lr 1e-3, 16 examples per step and per forward pass, cosine, 3% warmup, seed 7) except 2 epochs (F1 peaked at 2) with a checkpoint every quarter epoch (8 checkpoints + step 0)
fixed.compute: RunPod RTX 4090 (no CTI-HAL uploaded; the selected checkpoint is scored on CTI-HAL on the laptop)

selection: as F1: the highest mean family top-1 over public dev and AnnoCTR dev; ties the earlier

success.headline: CTI-HAL family top-1: F2 minus F1 (same 968 statements), paired 95% CI lower bound above 0
secondary: AnnoCTR test family top-1: F2 minus F1, CI lower bound above 0

public test family top-1: F2 minus F1, CI lower bound above 0, reported overall and without TRAM (TRAM shares the most text with ATT&CK procedures, so an overlap that survived the filter would show there first)
success.reported: family micro-F1 top-1 and under the amendment-3 rule of the parent (threshold 0.25, not re-tuned); CTI-HAL family top-1 on statements whose gold family had fewer than 20 rows in F1's training data; F2 against B3, pipeline rank-1 and Jev C1 as for F1

stop_rules: more than 1% of a split's cases end in error
confirmation_runs: the selected checkpoint once on CTI-HAL, public test and AnnoCTR test; nothing is chosen, refit or rerun because of a confirmation result
adoption: none: an experiment, no product wiring
informed_by: F1's dev curve and confirmation results; F1's dev error analysis (about 12% of its dev errors on families with fewer than 20 training rows); the overlap-filter counts above. No F2 model exists.
